newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products - light ends, fuel steady.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products - light ends, fuel steady.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Monday with gas oil pressured by lower benchmark futures while gasoline remained steady in a fairly balanced market, traders said.
Lacklustre local gasoline demand balanced lower supply due to refinery turnarounds in the region as well as strong demand from the East. Demand out of Slovenia for April was also reported.
Naphtha prices were firm but a lack of material stifled business. Strong demand from the Far East has close to drained the market of cargoes for March.
Gas oil started to show some pressure around the edges although premiums held against futures which dropped $2 a tonne.
Local demand appeared restricted to Greece and Lebanon, but interest from Asia, South America and India has kept the market bouyant, traders said.
"But if that demand goes, so will the strength," said one Med trader.
Russian cargoes were heard offered around fob high quotes +$2-3, unchanged from Friday, but few buyers were seen.
Non-Russian 0.02 pct material was harder to determine, but talk was of offers around high fob quotes +$3-3.50.
Diesel held around flat cif high EN590 quotes.
High sulphur fuel oil cargo prices were stable with no trade seen and little interest. Players said continued good supply of stock was weighing down values.
"The feeling is the market is stable to lower," said one dealer.
Low sulphur prices were notionally firmer with limited supply. But traders said demand was just as weak and the trades needed to give the market direction were unseen.
